s1.syndrome_frame: Enlarging, painful, purplish mass in the ear canal with granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells
salient_findings: Purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
Irregular, friable surface with bleeding on minimal contact
Lobulated mass extending into the external acoustic canal and parotid space
Bilateral cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
Marked vascularity of the mass
key_facts: 7-year-old girl
2-year history of an enlarging mass
Intermittently painful
Purplish lump in the left ear canal
Cracking and pus-filled sores at the site 18 months earlier
Received antibiotics and analgesics before referral
3.5 × 2.5 cm purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
Irregular, friable surface with bleeding on minimal contact
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a lobulated mass in the cutis and subcutis
Mass extended into the external acoustic canal and parotid space
Bilateral level II–IV cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
CT angiography demonstrated marked vascularity of the mass
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with rapid growth, matching the 2-year history of an enlarging mass

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells on biopsy, consistent with LCH

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Highly vascular tumor with rapid growth, matching the CT angiography findings

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral cervical lymph nodes and atypical cells on biopsy, raising suspicion for lymphoma

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Marked vascularity on CT angiography and purplish-red mass, consistent with angiosarcoma

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Purplish-red mass and granulomatous inflammation, although less common in pediatric patients

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and atypical cells on biopsy, although typically presenting with lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Slow-growing tumor with friable surface, although less likely given the rapid growth and vascularity

raw.rationale: The presence of a rapidly enlarging, painful mass with atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation, along with the patient's age and the mass's location and vascularity, are consistent with Rhabdomyosarcoma, a common malignant tumor in children.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple lesions and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: More commonly affects bones and has a distinct histological appearance

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Would likely present with more pronounced lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Rare in children and typically has a more aggressive clinical course

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Strongly associated with immunosuppression, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, which are not prominent in this case

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: A rare tumor that typically presents as a slow-growing mass, which does not match the rapid growth described in the vignette
